overview.question: How far does the second candle move adversely from its own open when it eventually closes in the reversal direction?
overview.takeaway: Larger settings generally permit larger adverse movement within successful second candles. Corrected complete-leg duration is a raw clock proxy; neither description is an observable live entry filter.
overview.population: ES 4/5/6, GC 6/10 and NQ 10/20 Range XV candles. Geometry conditions on the following candle’s eventual same-direction close.
overview.qualification: Historical import, unreviewed during consolidation. Future-close conditioning, missing original inputs and unverified clocks prevent causal entry or execution claims.
overview.method: Second-candle adverse movement is measured from its own open to its adverse extreme, conditioning on eventual same-direction close. Complete-leg duration includes the reversal and same-colour successors, excludes right-censored legs, and uses raw timestamp differences. Tied-clock zero is observed and remains distinct from missing. Saved 95% mean intervals use export-date cluster draws.

statistics.label: ES 4 · median adverse move
statistics.context: 12,624 eventual same-direction second candles from 16,730 eligible next bars. Product ticks from the second candle’s own open; no median interval is supplied.

statistics.label: NQ 10 · median adverse move
statistics.context: 97,350 eventual same-direction second candles from 128,384 eligible next bars. This future-close-conditioned geometry is not an entry-time filter.

statistics.context: Among 8,095 qualified complete legs with at least three candles including the reversal; raw-clock zero is an observed duration, not missing.

findings.text: Larger chart settings generally allow larger adverse movement in the second candle that eventually closes with the reversal.
Duration summaries condition on complete legs of at least three candles and preserve tied-clock zero durations.
The eligible-next-bar count and same-direction rate expose the future-close selection used for geometry.

overview.method: The quality stack requires a body of at least seventy percent of range, a favourable close in the final twenty percent, and a break of the previous directional extreme. overview.question: Do VWAP state persistence, opposing slopes and the VWAP–TWAP comparison predict different next-thirty-minute outcomes?
overview.takeaway: State and slope gaps shrink after matching. The primary pooled fair-price comparison favours VWAP, but local-anchor checks favour TWAP; no universal reference preference or trading rule follows.
overview.population: ES, NQ and GC two-minute landmarks. The probability atlas uses the saved pooling; fair-price error comparisons retain separate products.
overview.qualification: All history is exploratory because outcomes had been viewed before the protocol. Matching is not causal adjustment; correlated landmarks and disagreeing anchor checks limit generalization.
overview.method: Persistent and rotational states use the preceding fifteen closes and crossing counts. Future residence follows evolving causal VWAP; prior thirty-minute slopes use frozen ATR-scaled cutpoints. Coarse shared-context matching retains unmatched observations. Frozen VWAP, TWAP and last-price errors target the same future median close. Saved shared-date 95% intervals are not adjusted for the three-question family.

statistics.label: State residence · matched gap
statistics.context: Persistent minus rotational next-thirty-minute residence: 96,078 matched candidate and 4,173 baseline landmarks. Saved 95% shared-date interval 15.5–22.0 pp.

statistics.label: Slope crossing · matched gap
statistics.context: Opposing minus aligned slopes: 28,420 matched candidate and 50,137 baseline landmarks. Saved 95% interval 1.0–3.2 pp; not family-adjusted.

findings.text: Raw state and slope gaps shrink after matching shared context.
The pooled primary fair-price comparison favours VWAP, while Asia and New York local-anchor checks favour TWAP.
Last-known price has smaller absolute error than either reference. Barrier follow-ups do not establish a trading rule.

limitations.text: Outcomes were viewed before the protocol; all available history remains exploratory rather than a pristine holdout.
Landmarks and products are correlated, and coarse matching is not a causal adjustment.

overview.question: What adverse, favorable and terminal GC movements follow a completed close below the outer lower EMA band?
overview.takeaway: The saved default shows different annual path scales, with separate adverse and favorable extrema. Neither MFE nor terminal-positive rates establish an executable exit or net profit.
overview.population: GC five-minute outer-lower-band signals; annual default at ten-bar cooldown and twenty-bar horizon, plus separately eligible 2026 horizons.

overview.method: A complete five-minute close at or below EMA225 minus three population residual standard deviations triggers a signal. The next contiguous full unadjusted five-minute open is the reference. Cooldown suppresses the following bars without restarting. Every outcome path must remain complete and within one contract/adjustment. Saved mean bounds use approximate 95% normal ISO-week cluster intervals, unadjusted for multiple comparisons.

statistics.label: 2026 · accepted signals
statistics.context: Saved annual default: ten-bar cooldown, twenty five-minute bars (100 minutes). Accepted signals include subsequently unavailable paths.

findings.text: Annual coverage, complete-path denominators and uncertainty differ; both adverse and favorable path extrema are retained.

Terminal movement is horizon-close minus next-open entry and is distinct from either path extremum.

Missing minutes, partial bars, gaps and roll/adjustment changes can make accepted paths unavailable.
